_meta.description: Tax tables for the M1 tax set (docs/engine-spec.md section 5). Rates are percents. Brackets are marginal: each 'from' is the taxable income above which that rate applies, and the last bracket runs to infinity. The engine reads tax numbers only from this file.
_meta.retrievedBy: Claude Code, from the documents cited in each section. Reviewed by Eli before use.

conventions.brackets: ascending list of { from, rate }; marginal; last bracket open-ended
conventions.stateMethod: Decision E9. M1 applies each state's brackets to income minus the state standard deduction where that deduction is a plain dollar amount. Personal exemptions, credits, local (city and county) income taxes, benefit recapture, and special provisions are not modeled until M2. States whose source is 'secondary' carry confidence lookUp until verified against the state's own revenue department in M2.

bracketsAndStandardDeduction.document: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, sections 4.01 (tax rate tables) and 4.14 (standard deduction)

fica.document: Social Security Administration, 2026 Cost-of-Living Adjustment Fact Sheet

additionalMedicare.document: IRS, Questions and Answers for the Additional Medicare Tax

earlyWithdrawal.document: IRS Tax Topic 558, Additional Tax on Early Distributions from Retirement Plans Other Than IRAs

hsaLimits.document: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-19, section 2.01; catch-up is statutory under IRC section 223(b)(3)

notes: Employee share shown. The employer pays a matching 6.2% and 1.45%.
Thresholds for the additional Medicare tax are not indexed.
The 12.4% portion stops at the Social Security wage base. The 2.9% portion has no cap. The additional 0.9% Medicare tax applies above the thresholds.
Exceptions (72(t), rule of 55, and others) are M2 strategies. M1 applies the penalty to every pretax or Roth-earnings withdrawal before 59.5.
Married filing separately Roth phase-out was not in the cited source and is left null until sourced.
The IRA limit is shared between traditional and Roth. Workplace limits cover 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457, and the TSP.
